findings.claim: Generated resolvers are not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. The change covers map, string-key, enum, and union formatter templates but leaves resolver generation unchanged, so generated resolver code can still skew coverage and the acceptance criterion that all generated code be decorated is not met.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedResolverCoverageAttributeTests.AllGeneratedTypesIncludingResolversAreDecorated. It generates both a formatter and a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] without configuring any setting, then requires every generated type to carry ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. On the current head it fails for resolver output.

questions.text: Does the scope of 'all generated code' include resolver output and its generated helper types, or only formatter classes?
options: Only generated formatter classes are in scope; resolver output is intentionally excluded.
Every generated type is in scope, including resolvers and their generated helper types.
questions.why_it_matters: The first option makes the formatter-only implementation scope-complete and removes the resolver omission finding. The second requires corresponding attribute emission in ResolverTemplate and any uncovered resolver helper declarations, making the omission a high-severity unmet acceptance criterion.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: 'All generated code' means the generated formatter classes only. Map, string-key, enum, and union formatters receive the conditional attribute unconditionally when the target supports it; resolver output remains unchanged and no setting is added.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: 'All generated code' means every emitted type, including resolvers and generated resolver helper types. As a minimal extension, ResolverTemplate must emit the same conditional attribute on its resolver and any uncovered generated helper declarations, still without requiring a setting.
